correlates.name: Methemoglobinemia (Slide 6)
correlates.presentation: Fatigue and a bluish tint to the skin.
correlates.pathophysiology: The central iron atom of heme is oxidized from the normal Fe2+ to Fe3+. Ferric heme is unable to bind oxygen.

correlates.name: Sickle Cell Hemoglobin, HbS (Slide 7)
correlates.presentation: A red cell packed with HbS has a lower oxygen-carrying capacity and destabilizes in shape, especially under oxygen-poor conditions, which wears the hemoglobin out much faster and causes a whole host of downstream problems.
correlates.pathophysiology: A point mutation in the hemoglobin beta chain substitutes valine for glutamic acid, slightly changing the conformation of the molecule.

correlates.name: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
correlates.presentation: The lecture's example patient was lucky — the exposure lasted only long enough to saturate about 50% of hemoglobin with CO. Anything more would produce a state not consistent with survival.
correlates.pathophysiology: CO competitively binds the same heme site as oxygen with 210-250x the affinity, forming carboxyhemoglobin and taking those binding sites out of service.
correlates.treatment: Regular air, about 5 hours; air saturated with O2, about 1.5 hours (raising the concentration gradient to drive CO off the binding sites); hyperbaric chamber at 3 atmospheres, about 20 minutes in extreme cases.

transporters.name: Band 3 Anion Exchanger
transporters.function: Carries out the chloride shift — bicarbonate generated inside the red cell leaves in exchange for chloride entering, preserving electroneutrality so CO2 carriage can continue
transporters.regulation: Runs in the opposite direction in the lung, where the whole sequence reverses to blow off CO2
transporters.inhibitor: Not a clinical target; carbonic anhydrase is the only red-cell-bound piece of the bicarbonate buffer system

formulas.name: Oxygen Binding Capacity
formulas.equation: 1 g of hemoglobin binds 1.34 mL O2
formulas.meaning: The maximum oxygen the hemoglobin present can carry, which is why anemia lowers oxygen content while leaving PO2 and saturation completely normal
formulas.normalValue: 15 g/100 mL x 1.34 = about 20.1 mL O2 per 100 mL blood

formulas.name: Oxygen Content
formulas.meaning: Total oxygen carried in all forms — about 98% bound to hemoglobin and 2% dissolved; the dissolved fraction alone supplies 15 mL/min against a 250 mL/min demand, a 13-fold shortfall
formulas.normalValue: Dissolved O2 = 100 mmHg x 0.003 = 0.3 mL per 100 mL blood

formulas.name: Oxygen Delivery
formulas.equation: DO2 = cardiac output x oxygen content
formulas.meaning: The quantity that actually matters at the tissue — it can fall from anemia, hypoxemia or low cardiac output, and treating the wrong one does nothing
formulas.normalValue: Requires roughly 250 mL O2 per minute at rest

formulas.name: P50 and the Dissociation Curve
formulas.equation: P50 = the PO2 at which hemoglobin is 50% saturated
formulas.meaning: The sigmoidal shape comes from positive cooperativity — saturated hemoglobin holds tightly while unsaturated hemoglobin releases easily, so the plateau protects loading and the steep limb favors unloading
formulas.normalValue: Unshifted P50 is about 25 mmHg; at PO2 50 mmHg hemoglobin is still about 85% saturated

formulas.name: Bohr Effect (Curve Shifts)
formulas.equation: Right shift: high PCO2, low pH, high temperature, high 2,3-DPG. Left shift: the reverse
formulas.meaning: A right shift raises P50 to about 40 mmHg so oxygen unloads more easily in exercising tissue; a left shift drops it to about 12.5 mmHg, favoring loading in the lung
formulas.normalValue: Applies to adult hemoglobin only — HbF does not interact with 2,3-BPG, which is how the fetus outcompetes maternal blood

formulas.name: Haldane Effect
formulas.equation: Deoxyhemoglobin binds CO2 and H+ more readily than oxyhemoglobin
formulas.meaning: In an exercising muscle three things reinforce each other: the curve right-shifts so oxygen comes off, the resulting deoxyhemoglobin carries more CO2, and that same deoxyhemoglobin buffers the H+ the bicarbonate reaction just made. All three reverse in the lung
formulas.normalValue: CO2 binds at a site distinct from the oxygen site, so the two are not competitive

formulas.name: CO2 Transport Fractions
formulas.meaning: CO2 enters the red cell, carbonic anhydrase makes carbonic acid, which dissociates to bicarbonate and H+; the bicarbonate leaves through band 3 in exchange for chloride
formulas.normalValue: Dissolved CO2 = 40 mmHg x 0.07 = 2.8 mL per 100 mL blood

formulas.name: Carbon Monoxide Affinity
formulas.equation: CO binds the heme oxygen site with 210-250 times the affinity of oxygen
formulas.meaning: Competitive displacement forms carboxyhemoglobin, and because CO never accumulates a dissolved partial pressure it stays diffusion-limited and keeps loading
formulas.normalValue: Clearance takes about 5 hours on room air, 1.5 hours on saturated oxygen, and 20 minutes at 3 atmospheres hyperbaric
